reforms.description: The Canadian government plans to harmonize the SR&ED tax credit for R&D activities across small and larger firms, addressing distortions caused by the larger credit for small firms.
reforms.growth_orientation_rationale: By reducing distortions in R&D funding, this reform is expected to enhance overall R&D investment and productivity in the private sector.
reforms.status_evidence: The government has announced plans to harmonize the SR&ED tax credit.
reforms.importance_rationale: This reform addresses a significant issue in the R&D tax credit system, which could lead to improved investment in R&D across firms of different sizes.
reforms.source_quote: Harmonise the SR&ED tax credit for R&D activities across small and larger firms, and consider reinstating capital costs in the credit base.

reforms.description: The government aims to make more use of direct grants to support R&D, particularly for digital technologies like artificial intelligence.

reforms.source_quote: Make more use of direct grants to support R&D, including to support digital technologies such as artificial intelligence.

reforms.description: Canada plans to increase gross domestic expenditure on R&D (GERD) by 0.5% of GDP over 5 years to reduce the gap to the OECD average by half.

reforms.source_quote: Increase gross domestic expenditure on R&D (GERD) by 0.5% of GDP to reduce the gap to the OECD average by half over 5 years.

reforms.description: Canada introduced a Digital Services Tax (DST) of 3% on digital services revenues, targeting businesses with significant global and Canadian revenues, aimed at enhancing tax fairness and generating additional revenue.
reforms.growth_orientation_rationale: The DST aims to create a fairer tax environment for digital services, potentially increasing government revenues that can be reinvested in innovation and public services.
reforms.status_evidence: The tax was enacted and applies to revenues earned since 2022.
reforms.importance_rationale: The DST represents a significant shift in tax policy aimed at the digital economy, addressing fairness in taxation and generating new revenue streams.
reforms.source_quote: Canada has moved ahead with the introduction of a Digital Services Tax (DST). It has enacted a 3% tax on digital services revenues in 2024.

reforms.description: The Housing Accelerator Fund was launched in 2023 to encourage municipalities to reform zoning laws to allow for higher-density housing, providing financial rewards for compliance.

reforms.description: The Canada Housing Infrastructure Fund was introduced in Budget 2024 to provide funding to municipalities for urgent infrastructure needs related to housing.

reforms.description: The federal government introduced a new co-operative housing development programme worth CAD 1.5 billion until 2028, offering access to forgivable and low-interest repayable loans to build and convert affordable rental co-operative housing.

reforms.description: Canada launched a CAD 100 million Codes Acceleration Fund in 2023 to help provinces, municipalities, and other stakeholders implement updated energy codes, facilitating faster adoption of energy-efficient building standards.

reforms.description: The federal government has committed CAD 3.8 billion through the Disaster Mitigation and Adaptation Fund to finance infrastructure projects aimed at reducing long-term risks from climate hazards.

reforms.status_evidence: The federal government has committed a total of CAD 3.8 billion through the Disaster Mitigation and Adaptation Fund.
reforms.importance_rationale: This significant investment in infrastructure projects addresses climate risks and enhances resilience, which is crucial for long-term economic stability.
reforms.source_quote: The federal government has committed a total of CAD 3.8 billion (or slightly over 0.1% of GDP in 2023) through the Disaster Mitigation and Adaptation Fund until 2033 to finance infrastructure projects designed to reduce long-term risks from climate hazards.

reforms.description: The federal government is allocating CAD 60 million over five years to accelerate the use of climate-informed codes and standards for resilient infrastructure, aiming to enhance the resilience of buildings and infrastructure against climate impacts.

reforms.source_quote: The federal government is allocating CAD 60 million over five years to accelerate use of 'climate-informed codes' and standards for resilient infrastructure.

reforms.description: The government is modernizing the Scientific Research and Experimental Development (SR&ED) tax incentives to increase the annual expenditure limit and capital phase-out thresholds, extend access to public corporations, and restore eligibility for capital expenditures.
reforms.growth_orientation_rationale: By enhancing tax incentives, the reform aims to stimulate R&D investment among firms, particularly small and medium-sized enterprises, thereby fostering innovation and productivity growth.

reforms.source_quote: The Fall Economic Statement 2024 proposed increasing the annual expenditure limit and capital phase-out thresholds of the SR&ED programme’s enhanced credit available to small- and medium-sized Canadian-controlled private corporations.

reforms.description: The government is establishing a new Canadian Innovation Corporation (CIC) to provide a national-scale platform for business R&D support, incorporating the Industrial Research Assistance Program (NRC IRAP) to help small businesses scale up their R&D efforts.
